Quick numeric result copy omits the unit and its superscript but preserves displayed numeric rounding; other copy commands remain open.

copy.result.meaning: Copies the targeted valid calculation result.
copy.result.context: Accepted through copying round 2: Ctrl+C on Windows / Cmd+C on macOS in the editor with no text selection copies the single ready displayed result entry, even if that entry groups several interpretations. Click copy targets the clicked entry. Numeric result copy omits the unit: 4m copies 4, and 5m/s copies 5. Preserve displayed numeric rounding, all shown digits, signs, numeral-system prefix/case and grouping; do not copy hidden precision or change working values. Formula selection copies the selected visible text, including units. If multiple displayed entries exist without selection, the shortcut leaves the clipboard unchanged and shows copy.chooseResult. Count all entries after display grouping, including horizontal overflow. Quick copy keeps the window, formula and cursor, restores input focus after a click and creates no history. Missing or stale results cannot be copied; keyboard selection of a particular result remains open. Enter confirmation is a separate accepted action: in quick mode with one ready displayed result, it records history and copies with the same payload rules, then starts empty input while keeping the window open. Enter never accepts a completion suggestion.
copy.result.location: Copy action for the current or clicked result. Quick input is in scope; exact targeting in calculation sheets and history remains to be specified.

copy.success.meaning: Confirms that the clipboard write succeeded.
copy.success.context: Feedback only after a result has actually been written to the clipboard successfully. Ctrl+C/Cmd+C and click quick copy preserve input and add no history. Full quick-mode confirmation success also requires saving history: Enter then starts empty input in the open window, while Ctrl+Enter on Windows / Cmd+Enter on macOS hides the window with empty input on the next invocation. This message confirms only the clipboard write and must not imply that a failed history write succeeded or that selected formula text was copied as a result. A confirmation failure preserves the formula, result and open window. Successful Enter also collapses expanded history; failure does not. Retrying an incomplete confirmation without changing the formula or calculation must not duplicate an already saved history entry; after full success, apply the command used for the retry. Operation order and recovery after restart remain architecture decisions. Exact feedback presentation remains open.
copy.success.location: Brief copy feedback associated with the input/result region and its accessible live region. Presentation when confirmation resets input or hides the window is to be verified.

copy.error.text: Could not copy the result. Try again.
copy.error.meaning: Reports that writing the result to the clipboard failed.
copy.error.context: Shown or announced only when writing a result to the clipboard fails, including shortcut/click quick copy and the copy step of Enter or modified-Enter confirmation. A failed quick-mode confirmation preserves the formula, result and open window and shows this brief error; it must not clear input or hide the window. Do not use this message for a history-save failure or claim success. Retrying an incomplete confirmation without changing the formula or calculation must not duplicate an already saved history entry; after full success, apply the command used for the retry. Operation order and recovery after restart remain architecture decisions. Failed confirmation also preserves the expanded history state. Copying a formula selection is a separate operation.
copy.error.location: Feedback area near the active result.

history.title.meaning: Names the list of past calculations.
history.title.context: Shown when the history view is expanded. Successful Enter confirmation in quick mode with one ready displayed result adds the calculation to history, copies its result, starts empty input and collapses expanded history. Arrow Up opens it again with the newest calculation nearest to the stationary input. Failed confirmation does not collapse history. The history expansion state on the next invocation after modified-Enter hiding is not yet selected. Copying round 7 fixes historical results at confirmation; changed constants or functions do not recalculate them. Recalling a formula into input calculates a new result with current definitions while preserving the original record.
history.title.location: Heading of the history region above the stationary quick input. Initially the newest entry is closest to the input; Arrow Up shifts the list downward into the console and Arrow Down shifts it upward.

history.entry.accessibleName.meaning: Proposes announcing a historical formula and its complete displayed set of saved results.
history.entry.accessibleName.context: Editorial accessible-name draft for a focused history entry. Copying rounds 7 and 8 accept storing the complete result set and showing the formula with all saved displayed answers in one horizontal row. The answer chosen at confirmation is bold when several answers exist; use the separate history.result.chosen description to make that distinction available without relying on font weight alone. Do not add visible interpretation captions, drop saved displayed alternatives or substitute the live recalculation. Exact list announcement and native accessibility behavior require prototype verification.

placeholders.expression: The historical mathematical formula, formatted for the active locale according to the existing unit-language rules. Do not translate or alter inserted user names or comments.
placeholders.results: The complete formatted set of saved displayed results for this history entry, including unit and numeral-system notation. Do not use the live recalculation or only the copied numeric value. List formatting and selection announcement are handled by the accessibility presentation and remain to be verified.

history.reuse.meaning: Recalls a previous expression for further input.
history.reuse.context: Used for a selected history entry. Accepted in copying round 7: the recalled formula is calculated anew with current user constants and functions; the original history record and its saved results remain unchanged. Navigation that recalls the formula does not itself confirm or create a new record. Successful confirmation records the new calculation under the existing Enter or modified-Enter flow. Retrying an incomplete confirmation with unchanged formula and calculation does not duplicate an already saved entry; copying round 8 accepts a separate record for every new successful confirmation, even when formula and results match an earlier record.
history.reuse.location: Actions associated with a history entry.

help.precedence.unitPowersRule.text: A final 2 or 3 on a complete known length-unit symbol automatically displays as a superscript: cm2 becomes cm², мм3 becomes мм³, ft2 becomes ft² and metre2 becomes metre². The same rule applies to explicit length aliases and to the Latin baseline plus one active locale. m2/m3 and м2/м3 always mean square/cubic metres, never minutes. Do not format a prefix of a longer name: m20 and m2rate remain unchanged; continuing the word removes the superscript formatting. Backspace immediately after m² deletes only the exponent, leaving m. Undo restores the preceding user input without an extra step for automatic formatting. Pasted formula text receives the same formatting as typed text: 2cm2 + 3cm2 displays as 2cm² + 3cm². One undo restores the state before the entire paste. Copying selected formula text puts the visible text on the clipboard, including actual ²/³ characters. Quick numeric result copy omits the unit and its superscript: 4m² copies 4. Displayed numeric rounding is preserved and the working value is unchanged. The caret ^ raises the entire quantity to a power: 2m2 denotes two square metres; 2m^2 leaves the supported answer 4m², discarding the squared-minutes interpretation. Unit support is checked after final cancellation. Shorthand autoformatting is not extended to time, mass or other dimensions.
help.precedence.unitPowersRule.meaning: Explains square/cube shorthand for all known length symbols, its whole-symbol boundary and editing behavior, while distinguishing quantity exponentiation.
help.precedence.unitPowersRule.context: Accepted through contextual-units round 9. Known length symbols include explicit metre/метр aliases and follow Latin-plus-one-active-locale availability. Formatting is based on a complete unit symbol, not a substring replacement inside an arbitrary name. The display rule does not approve the semantic parsing of m20 or choose a storage format. Round 9 approves identical formatting for pasted formula text, one undo for the entire paste and visible superscript characters when copying selected formula text. Backspace deletes the exponent and formatting adds no separate undo step. The metre/minute ambiguity is absent from square/cube unit shorthand. Copying round 2 omits units and their superscripts from quick numeric result copy while preserving displayed numeric formatting and working precision. Selected formula text still includes units and superscripts. Other copy commands, editing boundaries, stored-name conflicts and branch-error policies remain open.

help.precedence.comparisonChains.text: A chain such as `1 < x < 10` compares neighboring values and requires every comparison to hold. It means `1 < x and x < 10`. Stop at the first false comparison; do not compare a Boolean intermediate result with the next number.
help.precedence.comparisonChains.meaning: Explains the accepted pairwise comparison-chain semantics and short-circuit behavior.

help.precedence.lazyUnitsRule.text: Lowercase m can mean a metre or a minute; the active Russian spelling м follows the same rule. Lazy resolution uses the whole formula, including outer parentheses. If multiple interpretations remain valid, show all distinct visible answers: 10m / 2s gives 5m/s or the unitless 300. Identical-looking answers appear once: 2m * 2 displays one 4m. Answers have no interpretation captions and remain in one row with horizontal scrolling when needed. Grouping the display does not discard original meanings or exact values. Explicit metre and min select a unit directly; the Russian equivalents are метр and мин. Ordering and copy selection remain open.

help.precedence.durationNotation.text: Short duration symbols are w, d, h, m, s and ms. Russian symbols are н, д, ч, м, с and мс. Days remain 24 hours and weeks remain seven days. Adjacent duration components add, with or without spaces: 1h30m and 1h 30m both equal 90 minutes. Components may appear in any order and repeat: 30m1h equals 90 minutes; 1h30m15m equals 105 minutes. Use an explicit * to multiply adjacent duration quantities. With only ambiguous m symbols, retain both valid readings: 1m30m and 1m 30m give 31 minutes as a duration sum and 30 square metres as a length product. This does not introduce addition of adjacent lengths. A compound duration is one value for surrounding operators: 1h30m * 2 equals 180 minutes, and -1h30m equals minus 90 minutes. An incomplete final component such as 1h30 keeps the result blank until its unit is entered. An explicit operator is required before a following quantity of a clearly different dimension: 1h30m2km reports a missing operator; write 1h30m / 2km to calculate pace. This boundary does not remove the two accepted readings of 1m30m or other accepted forms of implicit multiplication.
help.precedence.durationNotation.meaning: Explains duration sums, accepted ambiguous readings, treatment as one value under surrounding operators, incomplete input and the boundary before another dimension.
help.precedence.durationNotation.context: Accepted through contextual-units round 7. Keep both operation readings and their values until whole-expression constraints are applied; do not force an ambiguous sequence to mean only duration. Examples describe value and dimension, not a new result notation or result caption. Original input is not automatically reordered. The explicit multiplication requirement applies to adjacent duration quantities, not to a duration followed by a parenthesized scalar expression. An unfinished 1h30 must not retain a stale answer or become multiplication by 30. A following quantity of a clearly different dimension requires an explicit operator. These duration rules do not regroup the separate length-product interpretation. Other token boundaries remain open.

help.precedence.minRule.text: The min function takes at least two arguments separated by semicolons. One complete expression in the following parentheses denotes minutes multiplied by that expression: 2min(2+4) equals 12 minutes. With no coefficient, one minute is implied: min(2+4) = 1min(2+4), or 6 minutes. Two or more arguments denote the function: 2 min(2;4) = 2 * min(2;4) = 4, without a unit. Spaces before min do not change the meaning. Count arguments at the current parentheses level: 2min(max(2;4)) has one outer argument and equals 8 minutes. While 2min(2; is incomplete, the result stays blank. Closing it as 2min(2;) produces a missing-argument error, without reinterpreting the list as minutes. The max function also requires at least two arguments. Other malformed argument lists are still being specified.
help.precedence.minRule.meaning: Explains how min distinguishes the minute unit from the minimum function by its outer argument count, including an implied one-minute coefficient and missing-argument states.
help.precedence.minRule.context: Accepted through contextual-units round 5, superseding one-argument functions min and max. Nested-call separators do not count as outer arguments. The explicitly accepted incomplete min list has no live result, and the closed list with a missing argument is an error. Do not reinterpret it as a minute product. Minute examples express value and dimension, not a new default output spelling. Other malformed lists remain open; this rule does not automatically allow every unit without a coefficient.

help.copy.quickRule.text: With no text selected, press {shortcut} to copy the only displayed current result. Numeric results copy the displayed number without its unit: 4m copies 4. Rounding, all shown digits, grouping and numeral-system prefixes are preserved. With text selected, the shortcut copies that selection, including its unit text. Click a result to copy it. When several results are displayed, the shortcut leaves the clipboard unchanged and prompts you to choose a result. The calculator stays open, your formula and cursor are preserved, and focus returns to input after a click. Quick copy does not add a history entry.

Count the entire grouped result row, including entries outside the horizontal viewport. For multiple entries without selection, preserve the clipboard and show copy.chooseResult. Unit omission applies to numeric quick-copy results, not selected formula text. Numeric prefixes are not units; localized logical results retain their previously approved displayed text. Exact result ordering, keyboard choice and feedback geometry remain open. This fragment does not add interpretation captions.

help.confirm.quickRule.text: With one ready displayed result in quick mode, press {shortcut} to record the calculation in history and copy the result. After both succeed, a new empty input starts in the same place, expanded history collapses and the calculator stays open. Arrow Up opens history again with the newest calculation nearest to the input. If saving history or copying fails, the formula and result remain and a brief error appears; the input is not cleared, history does not collapse and the window stays open. Numeric results are copied without units, using the displayed number. Ordinary quick copy keeps your current input and does not add history.
help.confirm.quickRule.meaning: Explains calculation confirmation and its immediate transition to a fresh input, distinguishing it from copying without confirmation.
help.confirm.quickRule.context: Accepted in copying rounds 3 through 5. The default shortcut is Enter in quick mode on both platforms. Full success records history, copies using the existing payload rules, collapses expanded history and focuses empty input in the fixed location. Failure preserves formula, result, open window and history expansion state and shows the appropriate brief error. Empty input has no ready result; do not retain or recopy the previous answer as its result. Enter does not accept completion suggestions. Modified-Enter confirmation is described in help.confirm.hideRule; help.confirm.retryRule explains accepted retry without duplicate history. Copying round 6 accepts the separate selection step for multiple answers; see help.confirm.multipleRule. Operation order, recovery after restart and expanded-mode behavior remain open.

Native shortcut and focus behavior still require the platform prototype.

placeholders.shortcut: The confirmation-and-hide shortcut in platform display form; accepted defaults are Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Cmd+Enter on macOS, in quick mode.

help.confirm.retryRule.text: If confirmation fails, retry without changing the formula or result to finish the same calculation. An entry already saved to history will not be added again. After saving and copying succeed, the command used for the retry determines whether the calculator stays open with empty input or hides until the next invocation.
help.confirm.retryRule.meaning: Explains retrying a failed calculation confirmation without adding a duplicate history entry.
help.confirm.retryRule.context: Accepted in copying round 5. Applies to retrying incomplete quick-mode confirmation of an unchanged formula and calculation, including when history was saved but clipboard copying failed. Changed formulas or results start a new confirmation. Copying round 8 distinguishes a new successful confirmation after full success: it creates a separate history entry even for identical formula and results. Enter on successful retry starts empty input and collapses history; Ctrl+Enter on Windows / Cmd+Enter on macOS hides with empty input on the next invocation. No atomic transaction or rollback of the system clipboard is promised. Operation order, persistence details and recovery after restart remain architecture decisions.
help.confirm.retryRule.location: Calculation confirmation section of application help, following the normal and hide confirmation explanations. Documentation only; no new retry button in the quick widget is approved.

help.confirm.multipleRule.text: When quick mode shows several results, press {confirmShortcut} or {hideShortcut} to focus the result row. The first answer is highlighted, but nothing is copied or saved yet. Use Left Arrow and Right Arrow to choose; the row scrolls when needed. Press {confirmShortcut} again to record the calculation and copy the chosen answer, then start empty input with history collapsed. Press {hideShortcut} instead to confirm and hide the calculator. Escape returns the cursor to its previous position in the formula without changes. Clicking an answer still only copies it and returns focus to input.
help.confirm.multipleRule.meaning: Explains choosing one displayed answer with the keyboard before confirming a calculation that has several results.
help.confirm.multipleRule.context: Accepted in copying round 6 for quick mode. Entry into selection does not record history, copy, reset input or hide; highlighting the first answer is navigation focus only. Completion closes without accepting a suggestion. The command used on the selected answer determines the successful transition. Existing numeric copy payload, confirmation failure and unchanged-calculation retry rules still apply. Selection of a grouped displayed answer does not discard hidden interpretations. This does not change Ctrl+C/Cmd+C in the formula editor or approve result captions. Copying round 7 accepts saving the complete result set and the displayed answer chosen at confirmation; see help.history.recordRule. The exact storage format, other keys in selection and focus after a result changes remain separate decisions; native focus and accessibility require prototype verification.
help.confirm.multipleRule.location: Calculation confirmation section of application help, after the single-answer and hide command explanations. Describes the existing result row; no new menu or button is added.

placeholders.confirmShortcut: The normal quick-mode confirmation shortcut in platform display form; the accepted default is Enter on Windows and macOS.
placeholders.hideShortcut: The quick-mode confirmation-and-hide shortcut in platform display form; accepted defaults are Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Cmd+Enter on macOS.

help.history.recordRule.text: History keeps the formula, all its results and the answer chosen when you confirmed the calculation. Copying one answer does not remove the others. Saved results do not change when you edit a constant or function. When you bring a formula back into input, it is calculated again using the current definitions; the original history entry stays unchanged. Bringing a formula back into input does not itself add a new history entry. Each new successful confirmation adds a separate history entry, even for an identical calculation. Retrying an unfinished confirmation after an error does not duplicate its saved entry.
help.history.recordRule.meaning: Explains what a history record retains and distinguishes viewing saved results from recalculating a recalled formula.
help.history.recordRule.context: Accepted in copying round 7. Records retain working values and hidden interpretations as well as the displayed answer chosen at confirmation, not merely the rounded unitless clipboard text. Historical values are not recalculated when definitions change; recalling a formula into input uses current definitions. Locale changes may redraw local unit symbols under the existing language rule without changing historical values. Copying round 8 accepts a row containing the formula and all saved displayed results, with the confirmation choice in bold and horizontal overflow; see help.history.displayRule. Every new successful confirmation creates a separate entry even for identical content; retrying an unfinished confirmation after failure must not duplicate its entry. This does not approve a new badge or button, automatic restoration of old definitions, or a serialization format.
help.history.recordRule.location: History section of application help, alongside the explanation of recalling calculations. Documentation text; the history row and its accessible presentation are specified separately.

history.result.chosen.meaning: Identifies the historical answer selected when the calculation was confirmed.
history.result.chosen.context: Editorial accessibility description for the saved selected answer when a history entry has several displayed answers. Copying round 8 accepts visual bold emphasis; this description communicates its meaning to assistive technology. It describes the original confirmation choice, not current keyboard focus or a later click. No visible interpretation caption or badge is added. Exact native announcement and integration with the full history entry require prototype verification.
history.result.chosen.location: Programmatic description of the chosen historical answer inside a history row; not visible text.

help.history.displayRule.text: Each history row shows the formula and all its saved results. With several results, the answer chosen at confirmation is bold. Long rows scroll horizontally. Moving through history does not change the saved choice.
help.history.displayRule.meaning: Explains the history row, its saved choice emphasis and access to long content.
help.history.displayRule.context: Accepted in copying round 8. All saved displayed answers are shown after the existing grouping of identical full formatted answers, retaining hidden interpretations. Interpretation captions remain absent. A single displayed answer needs no additional choice emphasis. Bold emphasis must preserve the existing dim fractional tail. Saved choice is distinct from current keyboard focus. Exact visual styling and accessibility remain subject to prototype verification.
help.history.displayRule.location: History section of application help, next to help.history.recordRule. Documentation only; no new history control is introduced.
